definition: Class of data specific to each cloud service customer (cf. below) that is required to administer the cloud service (cf. below). Account data (e.g. payment information, contact information, etc.) is typically generated when a cloud service is purchased and is under the control of the cloud service provider (cf. below).
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: In this criteria catalogue, this term is used synonymously with the term ‘system components’ (cf. below).
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Feature of information in which changes can be uniquely assigned to an originator.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The property that information, services, and functions of an IT system, IT applications or IT networks are accessible and usable on demand by an authorised entity.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Paradigm for enabling network access to a scalable and elastic pool of shared physical or virtual resources with self-service provisioning and administration on-demand. Examples of resources include servers, operating systems, networks, software, applications, and storage equipment. Self-service provisioning refers to the provisioning of resources provided to cloud services performed by cloud service customers through automated means.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Information technology service offered via cloud computing. This includes infrastructure (e.g. computing power, storage space), platforms and software.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A cloud service broker is a natural or legal person, or a group of either (whether or not incorporated), that performs a set of specified tasks supporting or auxiliary to the cloud service provider, one or more cloud service customer, or both — with the specific function of negotiating relationships between cloud service customers and cloud service providers.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Natural or legal person who has a business relationship with the cloud service provider for the purpose of using the cloud service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Class of data objects under the control, by legal or other reasons, of the cloud service customer that were input to the cloud service (including credentials to control access to information or other resources), or resulted from using the functionalities of the cloud service by or on behalf of the cloud service customer via the published interface of the cloud service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Class of data objects under cloud service provider control that are derived as a result of interaction with the cloud service by the cloud service customer. Cloud service derived data includes the portion of log data containing records of who used the service, at what times, which functions, types of data involved and so on. It can also include information about the numbers of authorised users and their identities. It can also include any configuration or customisation data, where the cloud service has such configuration and customisation functionalities.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Natural or legal person providing a cloud service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Class of data objects, specific to the operation of the cloud service, under the control of the cloud service provider. Cloud service provider data includes but is not limited to configuration and utilisation information of system components, storage and network resource allocations, physical and virtual resource failure rates, operational costs and so on.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Natural person, or entity acting on their behalf, associated with a cloud service customer that uses cloud services.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The property that information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorised individuals, entities, or processes.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Cybersecurity risks are effects of uncertainty associated with information and technology. Cybersecurity risks relate to the loss of confidentiality, authenticity, integrity (cf. below), or availability of information, data, or information systems. They reflect potential adverse impacts to organisational operations (i.e., mission, functions, image, or reputation) and assets, in particular with regards to the security of network and information systems.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A framework is a structured set of policies, procedures, guidelines and accompanying documents that provide an organised approach for archieving specific objectives.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Functional building block needed to engage in an activity, backed by an implementation.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A guideline provides recommendations, orientation and good practice about a specific topic. They are less formal than policies or procedures (both cf. below) and do in general not exhibit requirements. They often serve as explanations for policies and help to set procedures.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: System components (cf. below) that are classified as hardware.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Physical and virtual infrastructure resources (e.g. servers, storage systems, network components), as well as end point devices if the cloud service provider has determined in a risk assessment that these could endanger the information security of the cloud service in the event of loss or unauthorised access (e.g. mobile devices used as security tokens for authentication).
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A service consisting fully or mainly in the transmission, storing, retrieving or processing of information by means of network and information systems.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Unplanned interruption to the cloud service, a reduction in the quality of the cloud service or an event that has not yet impacted the cloud service to the cloud service customer.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Information security refers to the practices and principles designed to protect information from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction. In the context of this catalogue, it ensures confidentiality, integrity, authenticity and availability of cloud service customer data, cloud service provider data, cloud service derived data and account data.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The property that information is complete, accurate (correct, undamaged) and protected from manipulation and unintentional or erroneous alteration.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A location is a single premises containing one or more data halls, each with separate power supply, network connectivity, and fire protection. Each location is physically separated from all other locations and is exclusive to a single zone.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A document used to record and describe or denote selected items identified during execution of a process or activity. Log data includes both cloud service derived data and cloud service provider data.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Time limit until which a business process may be unavailable before intolerable consequences arise for an organisation. The time limit is determined based on a damage assessment of the affected business process.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Capacity required in an emergency to ensure adequate business operations. The MBCO is determined individually for each business process or resource.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A partition is an overarching grouping of regions (cf. below) that share a unified identity and access management (IAM) system for both cloud service provider personnel and customers. Each region is exclusively part of one partition, and there is strict separation without shared infrastructure between partitions.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Authorised, simulated real-world attack of system components for identifying ways to exploit vulnerabilities to circumvent or defeat the security features of the cloud service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Intentions and directions of an organisation that are formally expressed by its top management.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A procedure is often connected to a policy and describes how a policy, process or task is put into concrete action; i.e. it operationalises the expectations that policies lay out.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Sufficient and adequate level of information security for the cloud service provider’s customers with respect to the information processed, stored or transmitted in the cloud service. The protection need of system components and data is inherited from the protection need of the cloud service. The cloud service customer has to decide for themselves whether or not the level of information security for the cloud service customer data, cloud service derived data and account data suffices according to their own protection need.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Maximum age that available data may have in order to enable the adequate operation of time-critical business processes after a disruption. The RPO is usually specified as the required frequency of data backups per application, IT system or business process.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The period of time following an incident within which a product, service or activity must be resumed, or resources must be recovered, to a predefined level, in order to limit the impact of the interruption to an acceptable level.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Availability of alternate components, systems, or processes to assume the intended function following the failure of one or more components, in order to maintain the required level of service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A region comprises one or more zones (cf. below), all situated within a single metropolitan area (metropole). Cloud service providers may use any name for a region, such as ‘EU-south-west’, but the region’s infrastructure must be confined to one metropolitan area and never dispersed as broadly as an entire Introduction
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Ability to resist, adapt to, or quickly recover from potentially disruptive events or conditions, whether natural or anthropogenic, in order to maintain or restore the intended service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Person or entity with the accountability and authority to manage a risk.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Event compromising the availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of stored, transmitted or processed data or of the services offered by, or accessible via, system components of the cloud service. An incident is a materialised cybersecurity risk. A security incident is a strict subset of incidents.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Addition, modification, or removal of system components (cf. below) that could reasonably be expected to materially impact information security risks, control effectiveness or contractual obligations of the cloud service provider. Exemplary events that could represent a significant change are listed in the supplementary information for criterion OPS-22.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: System components (cf. below) that are classified as software.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Elements of information and communication technology systems required for the information security of the cloud service during the creation, processing, storage, transmission, deletion or destruction of information in the cloud service provider’s area of responsibility, which may be classified into the following five categories: infrastructure, software, people, procedures, and data.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Done or occurring sufficiently early, without unreasonable delay, considering the nature of the matter and the potential harm it could cause, including the cloud service provider’s ability to meet the C5 criteria.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Use of a variety of automated tools combined with manual verification of identified issues to identify, assess, and report vulnerabilities that, if exploited, may result in intentional or unintentional compromise of the cloud service and its data.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: A zone is a logical group consisting of at least two locations in close proximity to each other. Zones are physically segregated with separate power supply, cooling, networking and environmental risk profiles, such as separate fire compartments, to minimise the risk that disruptions at one zone impact the availability of other zones within a region.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: An assurance engagement in which a party other than the practitioner (cf. below) measures or evaluates the underlying subject matter against the criteria. A party other than the practitioner also often presents the resulting subject matter information in a report or statement and concludes whether or not the subject matter information is free from material misstatement (cf. below). Please note: In general usage, assurance engagements are called audits, whereas public accountants use the term audit for financial statement audit engagements, only. To ease understanding also for general readers, we use the term audit in the description to refer to general usage although it is not an audit engagement of a financial statement but an attestation engagement.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The criteria applied to assess the information security of the cloud service and defined in this catalogue.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Method of addressing the services provided by a subservice organisation (cf. below) in which the components of the subservice organisation’s system of internal control (cf. below) used to provide the services to the cloud service provider are excluded from the description of the cloud service provider’s system of internal control relevant to the development and operation of the cloud service, and from the scope of the audit. Consequently, no information provided about the subservice organisation beyond the information obtained by the cloud service provider for the operation of its controls to meet the criteria of the SSO domain is considered in the audit. However, the description of the system of internal control identifies (a) the nature of the services performed by the subservice organisation; (b) the types of controls expected to be performed at the subservice organisation that are necessary, in combination with controls at the cloud service provider, to provide reasonable assurance that the applicable C5 criteria were achieved; and (c) the controls at the cloud service provider used to monitor the effectiveness of the subservice organisation’s controls.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Information declared by the cloud service provider.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Controls (cf. below) that a cloud service provider assumed, in the design of its system of internal control (cf. below) relevant to the development and operation of the cloud service, would be implemented by cloud service customers (user entities). The implemented complementary user entity controls together with the cloud service provider internal controls are necessary to provide reasonable assurance that the applicable C5 criteria are met.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Controls (cf. below) that cloud service provider assumed, in the design of its system of internal control (cf. below) relevant to the development and operation of the cloud service, would be implemented by the subservice organisation (cf. below). The complementary subservice organisation controls together with the Introduction
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Policy or procedure to reduce the likelihood of events occurring or to detect events that have occurred in order to maintain the information security of the cloud service. Controls exist within each of the five components of the cloud service provider’s system of internal control (control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication and monitoring activities). A control is either preventive (designed to avoid an unintended event or result at the time of initial occurrence) or detective (designed to discover an unintended event or result after the initial processing has occurred, but before the ultimate objective has concluded, and with action taken to correct or avoid an unintended event our result).
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Actions established by policies and procedures to help ensure that management directives to mitigate risks to the achievement of objectives are carried out.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Set of standards, processes and structures that provide the basis for carrying out internal control across the organisation.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Term used to identify misstatements resulting from controls that were not suitably designed or did not operate effectively.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Term used to identify misstatements resulting from the failure of a control to operate in a specific instance. A deviation may, individually or in combination with other deviations, result in a deficiency.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: An audit engagement in which the practitioner (auditor) audits the cloud service as the underlying subject matter against the C5 criteria and presents the resulting subject matter information as part of its reporting.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Method of addressing the services provided by a subservice organisation (cf. below) in which the description of the cloud service provider’s system of internal control (cf. below) relevant to the development and operation of the cloud service includes a description of (a) the nature of the services provided by the subservice organisation; (b) the components of the subservice organisation’s system of internal control used to provide services to the cloud service provider, including the subservice organisation’s controls that are necessary, in combination with controls at the cloud service provider, to provide reasonable assurance that the applicable C5 criteria were met; and (c) the controls at the cloud service provider used to monitor the effectiveness of the subservice organisation’s controls. (When using the inclusive method, controls at the subservice organisation are subject to the auditor’s test procedures. Because the subservice organisation’s system components are included in the description, those components are included in the scope of the audit.)
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Information is necessary for the entity to carry out internal control responsibilities in support achievement of its objectives. Communication occurs both internally and externally and provides the organisation with the information needed to carry out day-to-day controls Introduction
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Deficiencies in the statement, e.g.: 1. Information does indicate that controls are not suitably designed, not implemented or not operating effectively to meet the C5 criteria with reasonable assurance; 2. Information is false or missing that may be individually or collectively relevant to the cloud service provider’s customers in order to assess the information security of the cloud service; or 3. Information includes inappropriate generalisations or unbalanced and distorting representations that may mislead the cloud service provider’s customers.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Ongoing evaluations, separate evaluations, or some combination thereof to ascertain whether each of the five components of internal controls is present and functioning.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The individual(s) conducting the audit, also referred to as the ‘auditor’. Risk assessment Process for identifying and analysing risks to achieving the entity’s objectives.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Partners, vendors, or other third parties that provide services to the cloud service provider associated with the development or operation of the cloud service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Service organisations for which the following characteristics apply in combination: 1. The services provided by the service organisation are likely to be relevant to the cloud service customers’ understanding of the applicable C5 criteria. A service is likely relevant, if the service organisation has access to system components of the cloud service and may access confidential information or transmit information between themselves and the cloud service. 2. Complementary subservice organisation controls (CSOC) at the service organisation are required in combination with the controls of the cloud service provider, to meet the applicable C5 criteria with reasonable assurance.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The principles, procedures and measures applied by the legal representatives (management) of the cloud service provider towards the organisational and technical implementation of management decisions to ensure the effectiveness and efficiency of business activities, the information security of the cloud service and compliance with the legal and other regulations applicable to the cloud service provider. This catalogue outlines criteria for the cloud service provider’s control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication and monitoring activities that are relevant to the development and operation of the cloud service.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The confirmation of a claim by the cloud service provider itself, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended future use or application have been fulfilled.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: The confirmation of a claim by the cloud service provider itself, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf

definition: Assertions on the description of the cloud service provider’s system of internal control and on the suitability of the design and, where relevant, operating effectiveness of the controls to meet the C5 criteria prepared by the legal representatives (management) of the cloud service provider.
source_document: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2026), Version 1.0.1, Federal Office for Information Security (Germany) - KB 2/Germany/BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.pdf
